title: Buddy Petit and Kid Rena, and the tune Sand Dunes
summary: Barnes describes Buddy Petit's playing, compares it with Kid Rena's treatment of Sand Dunes, and likens early Armstrong to Petit.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: You ever worked with Buddy Petit?
What was he like to work for?

Buddy is a wonderful trumpet player. But he played different from Kid Rene, in that he liked to run a lot of different, we used to call that changes, because of his horn. But if you would hear Louis Armstrong's old record, just like listening to Buddy Petit. But I don't mean Louis' late record, where he played all high in his pretty well. In the beginning, when he first started playing, he started to record in the ring of 20s, that you could get some of the records, you'd listen to Buddy Petit. Yeah.

You said that, remember that number we recorded the other day, Sand Dunes? You said that was one of Buddy's numbers? Is that where you first heard that number? By Buddy playing it? Did I? That number we recorded the other day, Sand Dunes. I understand. Is that where you first heard that number, by Buddy Petit playing it, or did you?
I first heard it with Kid Rene. But I did hear Buddy play it too. But Kid Rene, I used to play that number, with Kid Rene. That was one of his main numbers.
You were saying yesterday, not yesterday, when we came by here last, you were explaining to us that Kid Rene used to play it differently to Buddy. Do you remember? That who?
Kid Rene used to play that song, in a different way to Buddy. Oh yeah. And how was it different?
Well, it wasn't much difference, but it was, Rene would run a few eight notes, and you'd pick up on that number. And Buddy Petit would make it simple, you know.
You'd make a 20 minute simple pickup. You know, I tell you about that. Rene would run a scale up to the beginning of the melody. Yeah.
